text: now we come to the chapter of the eights 8 things 8.1.2 is an important suta also monks there are these 8 conditions 8 causes conducive to getting wisdom not yet gotten as to first things in holy living and when got into making it become more to its development so that it is made become made perfect what aid hearing among dwells near the teacher or some companion in the holy life whom he regards as teacher so that he is firmly established in conscientiousness fear of blame or a sense of remorse love and respect this is the first condition the first cause conducive to getting wisdom consciousness this is the eighth condition the eighth cause conducive to getting wisdom not yet gotten as to first things in holy living and when gotten to making it become more to its development so sense of conscience and fear of blame or a sense of remorse if he does anything wrong and also love for the teacher and respect for the teacher is the first condition the second 1 is since he has a teacher then he frequently asks anything that he does not understand that is in doubt he asked so that the teacher explains to him the meaning and the third 1 he strives in 2-fold seclusion that of body and and that of mind bodily situation is to be um physically secluded from other people either a person can live in a forest monastery or the person can live in any monastery but but to be a bit aloo from other people not to mix too much with other people or talk with other people [Music] but the highest form of bodily seclusion is to live alone from uh from from everybody here to live in a forest on a cave alone and then that would be the highest degree of bodily seclusion mental seclusion is to be secluded from the developments that means to practice meditation so that the mind attains conditions obsess the world the world revolves around these 8 worldly conditions 1 a gain and loss fame and dishonor praise and blame happiness and suffering monks these 8 worldly conditions obsess the world and the world revolves around these 8 worldly conditions i'll just stop here for a moment these 8 conditions uh worldly states early conditions roka dhamma and chinese they have in the chinese buddhism they are called the 8 winds 8 winds which move a person will shake the person [Music] and then the buddha continued monks to the unlearned common average folk come gain loss fame dishonor praise blame happiness suffering to the learned aryan disciple also come gain loss and so forth here then monks what is the distinction what is the peculiarity of and what is the difference between the aryan disciple and the common average vote god our doctrines have their foundation and the exalted 1 they are guided by the exalted 1 they have the exalted 1's protection well indeed worried for us if the exalted 1 would expound the meaning of his speech to us then when the monks have heard the exalted 1 they will treasure his words in his in their hearts and the buddha said then listen monks give heed i will speak yes lord they replied and the exalted 1 said monks gain comes to the unlearned common average folk who reflect not thus this gain which has come is impermanent painful and subject to change they know it not as it really is similarly lost comes fame dishonor praise blame happiness suffering they reflect not that such are impermanent painful and subject to change nor do they know these conditions as they really are gain loss and so forth take possession of their minds and wholes way there they welcome the gain which has arisen they rebel against loss they welcome the pain which has arisen they rebel against this honor they welcome the praise which has arisen they rebel against blame they welcome happiness which has arisen they rebelled against suffering thus given over to compliance and hostility they are not free from being born ageing dying sorrow lamentation pain grief and despair i say such folk are not free from ill but to the learned aren't disciple just the converse is the case and that's the end of the suta so here these 8 conditions they all come to us we all experience them but an ordinary person when he experiences these things he's moved by them when what he considers is good now like gain comes he's very happy but when loss comes he's very sad and these things gain loss etc take possession of of his mind and moves his mind very much he's moved very much by likes and dislikes and so because of that now you find this person most people ordinary people and they have this monkey mind who is always happy and sad and excited most of the time and the only way to overcome this like and dislike is in is is mentioned in the saka pandha sutra in the deega nikaya where sakha devaraja asked the buddha what is the cause of people quarreling and fighting in this world and the buddha said in gree and jealousy and then raja asked what is the cause of greed and jealousy and the buddha said i think i can dislike learning and the cause of life and dislike is desire and the cause of desire is thinking and the cause of thinking is proliferation of thoughts and how to stop the proliferation of thoughts and then the buddha said there's 2 types of happiness 1 is that 1 type of happiness is the happiness of thinking another type of happiness is the happiness that comes from not thinking and the the happiness that comes from not thinking is the happiness that is that comes from the jhana janik bliss when the person attains the second jhana upwards the mind stops thinking and that kind of happiness is superior to the normal happiness that comes from thinking people get a lot of happiness from thinking that's why some people like to day dream they like to fantasize uh they they they like to imagine and there's only a type of happiness which which is higher than this which is charming bliss and so the way to overcome these likes and dislikes is to attain the bliss of jhana so that then we can overcome the likes and dislikes the next utah is 8.1.8 once the verbal uttara dwelt near mahi savatu on the sankey yaka mountain in dava jalika there the venable uttara addressed the monk saying proven says well it is for a monk to review from time to time his own faults well it is for him to reveal the faults of another well it is to review his own attainments well it is to review another's now at that time the royal deva where savannah was on his way from the northern region to the south on some business or other and he heard the verbal uttara teaching the monks this doctrine in dava jalika then just as a strong man might stretch forth his bent arm or might bend his outstretched arm even so the royal deva savannah disappeared from dava jalika and appeared among the devas of the 33 and v savannah approached sakha devaraja and said your grace i would have you know that this verbal uttara in [Music] teaches this doctrine well it is from time to time to review 1's own faults well it is to review another's well it is to review 1's own attainments well it is to review another's then as a strong man might bend and stretch out his arm again saka king of the devas disappeared from among the devas certainly they were king but pray sir is this the verbal uttara's own saying or is it the word of that exalted 1 arahan buddha now deva king i will give you an analogy for it is by analogy that men of intelligence understand the meaning of what he said imagine o king a great heap of grain near some village or market town from which country folk carry away corn on bingos or in baskets in lab or hand and if 1 should approach the fruit and question them saying from where i bring you this corn how would those folk in explaining best explain they would best explain the matter sir by saying we bring it from that great heap of grain even so o king whatsoever be well spoken all that is the word of the exalted 1 arahan buddha holy base thereon is both what me and others say it is marvelous it is wonderful sir how truly this has been said by the vulnerable uttara whatsoever be well spoken all that is the word of the exalted 1 buddha holy base thereon is what we and others say and then saka devaraja continued said once not long after the the departure of devadatta the exalted 1 was dwelling on vultures peak near raja gaha then the exalted 1 spoke thus to the monks concerning devadatta monks well it is for a monk to review from time to time is own false well it is for a monk to review from time to time another is false well it is for a month to review from time to time his own attainments relatives for among to review from time to time another's attainments monks mastered by 8 wrong states devadatta with his mind out of control became 1 doomed to suffer in hell in perdition dwelling there for a kalpa as a world cycle irreprievable by 1 aid mastered by gain by loss by fame by obscurity by honor by lack of honor by evil intentions by evil friendship with his mind out of control devadatta became 1 doomed to suffer in hell in perdition dwelling there a kappa irreprievable master by these data became irreprievable monks well it is that a monk should live mastering gain loss fame obscurity honor lack of honor evil intentions and evil friendship which arise and why and for what good purpose should a man live mastering gain loss and such states which arise nuns when a man lives with gain love's fame obscurity honor lack of honor evil intentions and evil friendship which arise unmastered there arise the ass of us full of distress and anguish but when those states are mastered those are full of distress and anguish are not for this good purpose monks a mom should master those states and so abide therefore monks train yourselves thus we will live mastering gain which arises mastering loss fame obscurity honor lack of honor evil intentions mastering evil friendship which arises train yourselves thus monks and then the saka devaraja told the venable uttara worthy uttara this is a dhamma discourse nowhere honored among the 4 companies namely the monks nuns and lay disciples both men and women sir let the verbal uttara learn by heart this dhamma discourse let him master this dharma discourse let him bear it in mind this dharma discusser is charged with good it is the first principle of holy living as the end of the sutta which is quite interesting because you see the monk is teaching dhamma and the devas they know and then when they know they discuss it among themselves and then saka devaraja came to talk with this tara which shows that the verbal uttara has some psychic ability here he can see the deva and talk to the deva and then this deva raja that the buddha spoke and he asked to teach the monks and nuns and lay disciples this suta many important sutas in this book now i come to 8.1.9 the buddha said monks 1 might say speaking rightly of nanda he is a clansman 1 might say he is strong 1 might say he is handsome 1 might say speaking rightly of him he is very passionate monks unless he keep the doors of the senses guarded be moderate in eating be watchful or wakeful unless he have mindfulness and self and awareness how can nanda live the holy life in all its purity monks this is the way for nanda to guard the doors of the senses monks if nanda has occasion to look to the eastern water concentrating his whole attention he gazes there at reflecting thus while i look to the eastern water they shall not flow in upon me covetousness nor discontent nor evil nor any unwholesome state thus in this way is he aware if he has occasion to look to the western quarter to the northern quarter to the southern quarter to the zenith to the nader to the points between the quarters concentrating his whole attention he gazes there at reflecting thus while i look to the points between the quarters covetousness and the rest shall not flow in upon me thus in this way is he aware monks this is the way for nanda to guard the doors of the senses monks this is the way of ananda to be moderate in eating monks herein nanda eats his food with orderly reflection not for amusement for lust for adornment for beauty but to suffice for the sustaining and nourishment of his body to appease hunger and to aid the practice of the holy life he reflects in this way i shall crush out the old feelings and not allow any new feelings to arise and i shall continue to dwell in blamelessness and comfort monks this is the way for nanda to be mounted in eating monks this is the way for nanda to watch fullness or wakefulness monks herein by day nanda purges his mind of thoughts that hinder when walking when sitting down so too during the first watch of the night during the middle watch he lies like a lion on his right side with foot covering foot mindful and aware intent upon the thought of getting up getting up in the last watch of the night he purges his mind of thoughts that hinder when walking and when sitting monks this is the way for nanda to watchfulness monks this is the way of ananda to mindfulness and awareness monks hearing to nanda recognize feelings rise recognize the endo recognize they said recognize perceptions rise recognize the endo recognize they said recognize reflections rise recognize the endo recognize they said monks this is the way for nanda to mindfulness and awareness monks unless nanda keep the doors of the senses guarded be moderate in eating be watchful unless you have mindfulness and awareness how can nanda live the holy life in all its purity as the end of the suta so we see in describing nanda who is supposed to be a half brother i think of the buddha said he's strong he's handsome he's very passionate so unless he keep he practice these few things unless he keep the doors of the senses guarded be moderate in eating be watchful or wakeful and have mindfulness and awareness it will be difficult for nanda to live the holy life in all its purity and concerning these few things that he has to practice for watchfulness or wakefulness and buddha said he purges his mind of thoughts that hinder and walking when sitting and then during the first watch of the night during the middle watch the first watch of the night is the time from 6 to 10 pm the middle watch is from 10 pm to 2 am and the last watch is from 2 am to 6 am and then the last part is for ananda to practice satisfaction you notice here the description of satisfaction is a little different from a few other sutas like in the satipatthana and the buddha describes satishan pajanya mindfulness and awareness the buddha described being aware of the bodily actions means when he's walking he knows he's walking when he's sitting he knows he's sitting when he's eating he's aware he's eating when he's changing his clothes he knows that he's changing his clothes or his ropes and whatever other bodily action but here the buddha is talking about mindfulness and awareness of the mind the working of the mind recognize feelings rise recognize the endo recognize they said recognize perceptions rise recognize they endure recognize they said recognize reflections or thoughts rise recognize the endure recognize they said so in other words here the other aspect of mindfulness and awareness is the watching the mind and in fact watching the mind is more important than the uh bodily actions uh when we are aware of the bodily actions it just helps to keep us mindful so that our mind is not scattered and but here when feelings perceptions and reflections or thoughts rise then we recognize them we are aware that we always have to remember concerning the body and the mind that these 5 kandas these 5 aggregates are not i not mine not myself so if you recognize these feelings these perceptions and these thoughts and we recognize them as not i not mine and not myself then we don't get uh we don't we we are not moved by them we are not swayed by them we adopt uh like uh an observer attitude now we just observe it with equinum equanimity then we see things as we as they really are instead of getting moved by the eu states yeah and now we come to the nexuta reproved evaded the question by another turned the issue aside and showed temper ill will and saltiness then the exalted 1 said to them eject this person monks throw out this person monks this person ought to be turned away monks why should other people plague you here in monks the going out coming in gazing up looking around stretching bending bearing of cloak ball and robe of that person seems just the same as the monks of worth so long as the monks see not his fault but when they see at once they know this is the very corruption of a recluse the chaff of a recluse the sweepings of a still further and away and why they say let it not corrupt the corn of war in just the same way monks some persons going out coming in and so forth seems just the same as the monks of worth so long as they see not his fault but when they realized this is the very corruption of every cruise the chavez were recluse the sweepings have a recluse they oust him from their midst so that he corrupt not the monks of earth monks suppose a man won some water pipes he enters a wood with a sharp axe and taps on this and that tree with the axe handle then those trees which are sound and have hearts when struck with the axe handle resound sharply while those rotten to the core sudden and moldy when struck give warth a hollow sound and such he at once cuts at the root then at the top and when he has done so he cleans out the inside until it is thoroughly clean then he joins the water pipes together in just the same way monks a person's going out coming in gazing up looking around stretching or bending bearing cloak a ball or rope is just the same as that of a worthy monk so long as the monks see not his fall but when they see they know at once this is the very corruption of a recluse the chaff of a recluse sweepings of a recluse realizing this they at once oust him from their midst and why they say let him not corrupt the other monks of worth that's the end of the sutta so in this suttas.sutta: 8.1.8 once the verbal uttara dwelt near mahi savatu on the sankey yaka mountain in dava jalika there the venable uttara addressed the monk saying proven says well it is for a monk to review from time to time his own faults well it is for him to reveal the faults of another well it is to review his own attainments well it is to review another's now at that time the royal deva where savannah was on his way from the northern region to the south on some business or other and he heard the verbal uttara teaching the monks this doctrine in dava jalika then just as a strong man might stretch forth his bent arm or might bend his outstretched arm even so the royal deva savannah disappeared from dava jalika and appeared among the devas of the 33 and v savannah approached sakha devaraja and said your grace i would have you know that this verbal uttara in [Music] teaches this doctrine well it is from time to time to review 1's own faults well it is to review another's well it is to review 1's own attainments well it is to review another's then as a strong man might bend and stretch out his arm again saka king of the devas disappeared from among the devas of the 33 and appeared before the verbal uttara in dava jalika and sakha the deva king approached the venerable uttara and saluted him and sat down at 1 side so seated he said is it true sir as they say that the venerable uttara teaches this doctrine to the monks namely well it is from time to time to review 1's own for to review anothers to review 1 owns attainments to reveal another's yes certainly they were king but pray sir is this the verbal uttara's own saying or is it the word of that exalted 1 arahan buddha now deva king i will give you an analogy for it is by analogy that men of intelligence understand the meaning of what he said imagine o king a great heap of grain near some village or market town from which country folk carry away corn on bingos or in baskets in lab or hand and if 1 should approach the fruit and question them saying from where i bring you this corn how would those folk in explaining best explain they would best explain the matter sir by saying we bring it from that great heap of grain even so o king whatsoever be well spoken all that is the word of the exalted 1 arahan buddha holy base thereon is both what me and others say it is marvelous it is wonderful sir how truly this has been said by the vulnerable uttara whatsoever be well spoken all that is the word of the exalted 1 buddha holy base thereon is what we and others say and then saka devaraja continued said once not long after the the departure of devadatta the exalted 1 was dwelling on vultures peak near raja gaha then the exalted 1 spoke thus to the monks concerning devadatta monks well it is for a monk to review from time to time is own false well it is for a monk to review from time to time another is false well it is for a month to review from time to time his own attainments relatives for among to review from time to time another's attainments monks mastered by 8 wrong states devadatta with his mind out of control became 1 doomed to suffer in hell in perdition dwelling there for a kalpa as a world cycle irreprievable by 1 aid mastered by gain by loss by fame by obscurity by honor by lack of honor by evil intentions by evil friendship with his mind out of control devadatta became 1 doomed to suffer in hell in perdition dwelling there a kappa irreprievable master by these data became irreprievable monks well it is that a monk should live mastering gain loss fame obscurity honor lack of honor evil intentions and evil friendship which arise and why and for what good purpose should a man live mastering gain loss and such states which arise nuns when a man lives with gain love's fame obscurity honor lack of honor evil intentions and evil friendship which arise unmastered there arise the ass of us full of distress and anguish but when those states are mastered those are full of distress and anguish are not for this good purpose monks a mom should master those states and so abide therefore monks train yourselves thus we will live mastering gain which arises mastering loss fame obscurity honor lack of honor evil intentions mastering evil friendship which arises train yourselves thus monks and then the saka devaraja told the venable uttara worthy uttara this is a dhamma discourse nowhere honored among the 4 companies namely the monks nuns and lay disciples both men and women sir let the verbal uttara learn by heart this dhamma discourse let him master this dharma discourse let him bear it in mind this dharma discusser is charged with good it is the first principle of holy living as the end of the sutta

its purity monks this is the way for nanda to guard the doors of the senses monks if nanda has occasion to look to the eastern water concentrating his whole attention he gazes there at reflecting thus while i look to the eastern water they shall not flow in upon me covetousness nor discontent nor evil nor any unwholesome state thus in this way is he aware if he has occasion to look to the western quarter to the northern quarter to the southern quarter to the zenith to the nader to the points between the quarters concentrating his whole attention he gazes there at reflecting thus while i look to the points between the quarters covetousness and the rest shall not flow in upon me thus in this way is he aware monks this is the way for nanda to guard the doors of the senses monks this is the way of ananda to be moderate in eating monks herein nanda eats his food with orderly reflection not for amusement for lust for adornment for beauty but to suffice for the sustaining and nourishment of his body to appease hunger and to aid the practice of the holy life he reflects in this way i shall crush out the old feelings and not allow any new feelings to arise and i shall continue to dwell in blamelessness and comfort monks this is the way for nanda to be mounted in eating monks this is the way for nanda to watch fullness or wakefulness monks herein by day nanda purges his mind of thoughts upon the thought of getting up getting up in the last watch of the night he purges his mind of thoughts that hinder when walking and when sitting monks this is the way for nanda to watchfulness monks
